::: {#sol-shared-memory}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
shared_array = pixels.copy()
shared = torch.from_numpy(shared_array)
shared[0, 0] = 99

copied_array = pixels.copy()
copied = torch.tensor(copied_array)
copied[0, 0] = 99

print(pixels[0, 0], shared_array[0, 0], copied_array[0, 0])
```

The [tensor](#def-tensor) from `torch.from_numpy` uses the array's own memory,
so changing the tensor changed the array, from `r py$pixels[1, 1]` to `r py$shared_array[1, 1]`.
`torch.tensor` copies the numbers, so its array kept `r py$copied_array[1, 1]`.
Sharing saves time and memory on large data,
at the cost of a change in one place showing up in the other.
The tensor method `.numpy()` shares memory the same way, in the other direction.

:::
